label: heart100-s2
summary: The model (training AUC 0.959) is a linear score plus gates added before a sigmoid. The largest part is the ST-depression pathway: switching it off lowers the training AUC to 0.847. In it a thallium-defect detector (on for 90 of the 90 patients with a reversible defect) and ST depression add up in unit 1946, so for the typical patient a reversible defect gives a predicted risk of 36% without ST depression (against 59% with a normal scan) and 77% at 1 mm. A flat ST slope raises the risk through unit 1476 (for the typical patient 88% against 59% with an upsloping segment), and a youth gate (on for 103 patients, more with a high maximum heart rate) lowers it. The direct terms (AUC without them 0.875) are led by the number of major vessels (1.11 per sd) and female sex (-0.91 per sd). An older-age brake (unit 3880, on for 84 patients) lowers the risk of older patients, and two hinges at high heart rates have a negligible effect. Worth checking: with a reversible defect the model gives younger patients a higher predicted risk (87% at 40 years against 36% at 65 years).
